race: Formula 1 Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, where Qatar's weekend is on and the championship talk gets properly spicy.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Spicy is right, because Mercedes are already sending chilli peppers from eventful Qatar practice, and the whole grid is paying attention.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Antonelli set the pace ahead of Russell, and the headline says second practice was disrupted, so the message is loud.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: So the car is quick, the mood is loud, and Verstappen is still finding ways to talk about Russell after Las Vegas.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Russell says the criticism is quite amusing, which is the calmest hot take in all of F1 and honestly very funny.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Meanwhile Hamilton says Ferrari are facing very challenging times, so the red car has a puzzle to solve before the weekend.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And Williams have blown through the cost cap by six hundred twenty seven thousand pounds, which is a wild footnote for a championship weekend.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Wild, but our top ten is built on form, track record, and who can handle Qatar's rhythm when the pressure rises.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Let's start with the big one, because Kimi Antonelli is our pick for first, and the confidence is high for a reason.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Championship leader, dominant season, and Mercedes have clearly clicked with this circuit, so the data is pointing the right way.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The history is a little thin, one race, average fifth, best fifth, no podium yet, but this is a new chapter for him.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: But the current form is the whole story, and when Mercedes set the pace, you do not sit on the fence, you just follow the silver.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I am not buying the fear, because the data says Mercedes are the team to beat, and Kimi looks like he can carry that badge.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Then I will take Max Verstappen for second, because this is his kind of place, and the confidence is high with good reason.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Qatar specialist, average first, best first, and three podiums across three races, which is almost scary consistent.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Recent wins, strong current form, and a driver who turns pressure into a routine, especially when the track suits him.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: How do you beat that, unless Mercedes are in another gear and Kimi just drives a perfect race?

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: You do not, because Max has the experience, the confidence, and the kind of pace that shows up when it matters.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: So George Russell is third, and yes, I know the podium history at this track is awkward, but the car is the story.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Three races, average fourth point seven, best fourth, and zero podiums here, so the track record is not singing.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: But he is a Mercedes, he has Qatar history, and he has been consistent in the top three, which is exactly what you want.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That is the real reason, not just the team badge, but the racecraft, the rhythm, and the fact he can defend a top three spot.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Now the deep cut, because Carlos Sainz is our tenth, the confidence is low, but the circuit history is doing the talking.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Low confidence, but this is his circuit, with a best finish of third here, and Qatar has a way of rewarding the patient.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: A Qatar specialist can score when the big teams are tangled, and that is a genuine gamble we are happy to take.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Plus Williams have a cost cap story, which keeps the weekend extra spicy, but the car is the only thing that matters on track.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Here is the full top ten in order, Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen, George Russell, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris, Lewis Hamilton, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Carlos Sainz.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Qatar is set, the championship is alive, the headlines are loud, and this could be the best race weekend in F1.
